properties.name: Kingdom of Alba Consolidation
properties.description: After Kenneth MacAlpin united the Scots and Picts in 843 CE, the Kingdom of Alba expanded eastward, consolidating Gaelic control over most of Scotland.

properties.name: Norse Viking Raids
properties.description: Norse Vikings raided and settled in western Scotland, Hebrides, and northern isles from 800-1263 CE, influencing local culture before their defeat at the Battle of Largs.

properties.name: MacRory/MacRuairidh Clan Territory
properties.description: The MacRory (Mac Ruairidh) name emerged in western Scotland as surnames became hereditary. Families settled in Ayrshire, Galloway, and surrounding regions.

properties.name: Wars of Scottish Independence
properties.description: The Wars of Scottish Independence (1296-1357) saw William Wallace and Robert the Bruce defend Scotland against English invasion, strengthening Scottish national identity.

properties.name: Protestant Reformation Spread
properties.description: The Protestant Reformation reached Scotland in 1560 under John Knox. Presbyterianism spread rapidly through western Scotland, profoundly influencing families like the McCrearys.

properties.name: Highland-Lowland Cultural Divide
properties.description: The Highland Line marked the cultural divide between Gaelic-speaking Highlanders and Scots/English-speaking Lowlanders. McCreary families emerged in the transitional western Lowlands.
